fullPassage: Merely convincing your children that worry is senseless and that they would be more content if they didn’t worry isn’t going to stop them from worrying. For some reason, young people seem to believe that worry is a fact of life over which they have little or no control. Consequently, they don’t even try to stop. Therefore, you need to convince them that worry, like guilt and fear, is nothing more than an emotion, and like all emotions, is subject to the power of the will. Tell them that they can eliminate worry from their lives by simply refusing to attend to it. Explain to them that if they refuse to act worried regardless of how they feel, they will eventually stop feeling worried and will begin to experience the contentment that accompanies a worry-free life.

questions.passage: Merely convincing your children that worry is (A)[senseless / sensible] and that they would be more (B)[content / miserable] if they didn’t worry isn’t going to stop them from worrying. For some reason, young people seem to believe that worry is a fact of life over which they have little or no control. Consequently, they don’t even try to stop. Therefore, you need to convince them that worry, like guilt and fear, is nothing more than an emotion, and like all emotions, is subject to the power of the will. Tell them that they can (C)[eliminate / increase] worry from their lives by simply refusing to attend to it. Explain to them that if they refuse to act worried regardless of how they feel, they will eventually stop feeling worried and will begin to experience the contentment that accompanies a worry-free life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) senseless=무의미한, (B) content=만족한, (C) eliminate=없애다
det.analysis:
✅ ① senseless — content — eliminate: 원문 일치. 걱정이 무의미하고(senseless), 걱정하지 않으면 더 만족스러울(content) 것이며, 걱정을 없앨(eliminate) 수 있다는 맥락 ←정답
❌ ② sensible — content — eliminate: (A) sensible(분별 있는)은 senseless(무의미한)의 반의어. 글은 걱정이 무의미하다고 하므로 부적절
❌ ③ senseless — miserable — eliminate: (B) miserable(비참한)은 content(만족한)의 반의어. 걱정을 안 하면 더 만족스럽다는 맥락과 모순
❌ ④ senseless — content — increase: (C) increase(늘리다)는 eliminate(없애다)의 반의어. 걱정을 없앨 수 있다는 맥락과 모순
det.tip: senseless(무의미한) / content(만족한) / eliminate(없애다)

questions.passage: Merely convincing your children that worry is senseless and that they would be more content if they didn’t worry isn’t going to stop them from worrying. For some reason, young people seem to (A)[believe / doubt] that worry is a fact of life over which they have little or no control. Consequently, they don’t even try to stop. Therefore, you need to convince them that worry, like guilt and fear, is nothing more than an (B)[emotion / decision], and like all emotions, is subject to the power of the will. Tell them that they can eliminate worry from their lives by simply refusing to attend to it. Explain to them that if they refuse to act (C)[worried / calm] regardless of how they feel, they will eventually stop feeling worried and will begin to experience the contentment that accompanies a worry-free life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) believe=믿다, (B) emotion=감정, (C) worried=걱정하는
det.analysis:
❌ ① doubt — emotion — worried: (A) doubt(의심하다)은 believe(믿다)의 반의어. 젊은이들이 걱정을 통제 불가한 삶의 일부라고 '믿는다'는 맥락과 모순
✅ ② believe — emotion — worried: 원문 일치. 걱정을 삶의 일부라 믿고(believe), 걱정은 하나의 감정(emotion)일 뿐이며, 걱정하는(worried) 척하기를 거부하라는 맥락 ←정답
❌ ③ believe — decision — worried: (B) decision(결정)은 부적절. 걱정은 guilt·fear처럼 '감정(emotion)'이지 결정이 아님
❌ ④ believe — emotion — calm: (C) calm(침착한)은 worried(걱정하는)의 반의어. '걱정하는 척하기를 거부하라'는 맥락과 모순
det.tip: believe(믿다) / emotion(감정) / act worried(걱정하는 척하다)

questions.passage: Merely convincing your children that worry is senseless and that they would be more content if they didn’t worry isn’t going to stop them from worrying. For some reason, young people seem to believe that worry is a fact of life over which they have little or no control. Consequently, they don’t even try to stop. Therefore, you need to (A)[convince / confuse] them that worry, like guilt and fear, is nothing more than an emotion, and like all emotions, is subject to the power of the will. Tell them that they can eliminate worry from their lives by simply (B)[refusing / choosing] to attend to it. Explain to them that if they refuse to act worried regardless of how they feel, they will eventually stop feeling worried and will begin to experience the (C)[contentment / anxiety] that accompanies a worry-free life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) convince=납득시키다, (B) refusing=거부하는 것, (C) contentment=만족감
det.analysis:
❌ ① confuse — refusing — contentment: (A) confuse(혼란시키다)는 convince(납득시키다)의 반의어. 걱정이 감정일 뿐임을 '납득시켜야' 한다는 맥락과 모순
❌ ② convince — choosing — contentment: (B) choosing(선택하는 것)은 refusing(거부하는 것)의 반의어. 걱정에 주의를 기울이기를 '거부함'으로써 없앤다는 맥락과 모순
✅ ③ convince — refusing — contentment: 원문 일치. 걱정이 감정임을 납득시키고(convince), 주의를 거부함으로써(refusing), 걱정 없는 삶의 만족감(contentment)을 경험하게 한다 ←정답
❌ ④ convince — refusing — anxiety: (C) anxiety(불안)는 contentment(만족감)의 반의어. '걱정 없는 삶'이 주는 것은 만족감이지 불안이 아님
det.tip: convince(납득시키다) / refusing(거부하기) / contentment(만족감)

questions.passage: Merely convincing your children that worry is ①<u>senseless</u> and that they would be more content if they didn’t worry isn’t going to stop them from worrying. Therefore, you need to convince them that worry, like guilt and fear, is nothing more than an ③<u>emotion</u>, and like all emotions, is subject to the power of the will. Tell them that they can eliminate worry from their lives by simply refusing to attend to it. Explain to them that if they refuse to act worried regardless of how they feel, they will eventually stop feeling worried and will begin to experience the ④<u>distress</u> that accompanies a worry-free life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 걱정 없는 삶이 주는 것은 만족감(contentment). distress(괴로움)는 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① senseless — 원문 일치. 글은 걱정이 '무의미하다(senseless)'고 설득하라는 내용이라 적절
❌ ② believe — 원문 일치. 젊은이들이 걱정을 삶의 일부라고 '믿는다(believe)'는 맥락에 적절
❌ ③ emotion — 원문 일치. 걱정은 죄책감·두려움처럼 하나의 '감정(emotion)'이라는 맥락에 적절
✅ ④ distress — 원문은 contentment(만족감). '걱정 없는 삶(worry-free life)'에 뒤따르는 것은 만족감인데 distress(괴로움)는 정반대라 모순 ←정답
det.tip: worry-free life가 주는 것 = contentment(만족감), distress(괴로움) 아님

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 걱정을 안 하면 더 만족스럽다(content). anxious(불안한)는 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① convincing — 원문 일치. 아이들을 '납득시키는(convincing)' 것만으로는 부족하다는 도입부 맥락에 적절
✅ ② anxious — 원문은 content(만족한). '걱정하지 않으면 더 만족스러울 것'이라는 맥락인데, anxious(불안한)로 바꾸면 '걱정을 안 하면 더 불안하다'가 되어 모순 ←정답
❌ ③ guilt — 원문 일치. 걱정을 '죄책감(guilt)·두려움'과 같은 감정으로 묶는 맥락에 적절
❌ ④ refusing — 원문 일치. 주의를 기울이기를 '거부함(refusing)'으로써 걱정을 없앤다는 맥락에 적절

questions.passage: Merely convincing your children that worry is senseless and that they would be more content if they didn’t worry isn’t going to stop them from worrying. For some reason, young people seem to believe that worry is a fact of life over which they have little or no control. Consequently, they don’t even try to stop. Therefore, you need to convince them that worry, like guilt and fear, is nothing more than an emotion, and like all emotions, is subject to the power of the will. Tell them that they can eliminate worry from their lives by simply refusing to attend to it. Explain to them that if they refuse to act <u>worried</u> regardless of how they feel, they will eventually stop feeling worried and will begin to experience the contentment that accompanies a worry-free life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 worried와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: worried=걱정하는 ↔ calm=차분한
det.analysis:
❌ ① anxious: anxious(불안한)는 worried(걱정하는)의 동의어
❌ ② distant: distant(멀리 떨어진)는 감정 상태가 아닌 다른 축이라 반의어가 아님
❌ ③ tense: tense(긴장한)도 worried와 같은 방향의 감정
✅ ④ calm: calm(차분한)은 worried(걱정하는)의 반의어 ←정답
det.tip: worried(걱정하는) ↔ calm(차분한)

questions.passage:
(A) Even when everyone else gave up, she refused to quit; her <u>will</u> to overcome the illness never weakened, and it inspired the whole team.
(B) After the wealthy man passed away, his lawyer read his <u>will</u> aloud so that the family could learn who would inherit the house and the land.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 will이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) will=의지, (B) will=유언(장)
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 의지 — (B) 습관: (A)는 병을 이겨내려는 '의지'로 맞지만, (B)는 상속 내용을 담은 '유언'이지 '습관'이 아님
❌ ② (A) 미래 — (B) 유언: (A)의 will은 미래를 나타내는 조동사가 아니라 명사 '의지(her will to overcome)'라 부적절
✅ ③ (A) 의지 — (B) 유언: (A)는 포기하지 않으려는 '의지', (B)는 변호사가 읽어 상속자를 알리는 '유언(장)' ←정답
❌ ④ (A) 유언 — (B) 의지: (A)와 (B)의 의미가 서로 뒤바뀜
det.tip: will: (A) 의지(volition) vs (B) 유언장(testament)

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a state of quiet happiness and satisfaction"

det.korean: contentment=만족감: 조용한 행복과 만족의 상태
det.analysis:
❌ ① anxiety: anxiety(불안)는 걱정·초조함이지 조용한 행복이 아님
❌ ② curiosity: curiosity(호기심)는 알고 싶어하는 마음이라 정의와 무관
❌ ③ boredom: boredom(지루함)은 만족과 반대되는 상태
✅ ④ contentment: contentment(만족감)는 '조용한 행복과 만족의 상태'라는 정의에 정확히 부합 ←정답
det.tip: contentment = 만족감 (a worry-free life가 주는 것)

questions.passage: Therefore, you need to convince them that worry, like guilt and fear, is nothing more than an emotion, and like all emotions, is subject to the power of the will. Tell them that they can eliminate worry from their lives by simply __________ (refuse) to attend to it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: refuse → refusing: 전치사 by 뒤에 오는 동명사
det.analysis: 동사 refuse를 동명사 refusing으로 바꿔요. 'by simply ___ to attend to it(단지 ~함으로써)'에서 전치사 by 다음에는 동사가 -ing형(동명사)으로 와야 하므로 refusing이 알맞아요.
det.tip: 전치사 by + 동명사(-ing). refuse → refusing

questions.passage: Tell them that they can eliminate worry from their lives by simply refusing to attend to it. Explain to them that if they refuse to act worried regardless of how they feel, they will eventually stop feeling worried and will begin to experience the contentment that __________ (accompany) a worry-free life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: accompany → accompanies: 단수 선행사 contentment를 받는 관계대명사절의 3인칭 단수 동사
det.analysis: 동사 accompany를 accompanies로 바꿔요. 'the contentment that ___ a worry-free life'에서 관계대명사 that의 선행사는 the contentment(단수)예요. 단수 주어에 맞춰 현재시제 3인칭 단수형 accompanies를 써야 해요.
det.tip: 단수 선행사 contentment → 관계사절 동사 accompanies (-y를 -ies로)

questions.passage: Merely convincing your children that worry is senseless and that they would be more content if they didn’t worry isn’t going to stop them from worrying. For some reason, young people seem to believe that worry is a fact of life over which they have little or no control. Consequently, they don’t even try to stop. Therefore, you need to convince them that worry, like guilt and fear, is nothing more than an emotion, and like all emotions, is __________. Tell them that they can eliminate worry from their lives by simply refusing to attend to it. Explain to them that if they refuse to act worried regardless of how they feel, they will eventually stop feeling worried and will begin to experience the contentment that accompanies a worry-free life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 감정은 '의지의 힘에 좌우된다(subject to the power of the will)'는 것이 글의 핵심
det.analysis:
✅ ① subject to the power of the will: 원문 일치. 걱정은 감정일 뿐이고 모든 감정처럼 '의지의 힘에 좌우된다'는 논지에 부합 ←정답
❌ ② beyond anyone's ability to change: '누구도 바꿀 수 없다'는 것은 걱정을 의지로 다스릴 수 있다는 글의 주장과 정반대
❌ ③ a fixed and permanent trait: 걱정이 '고정된 영구적 특성'이라면 없앨 수 없으므로 글의 논지와 모순
❌ ④ unrelated to our daily choices: 걱정이 의지·선택과 관련 있다는 글의 흐름과 어긋남
det.tip: like all emotions, is subject to the power of the will = 의지로 다스릴 수 있음

ch: subject to the power of the will

questions.passage: Merely convincing your children that worry is senseless and that they would be more content if they didn’t worry isn’t going to stop them from worrying. For some reason, young people seem to believe that worry is a fact of life over which they have little or no control. Consequently, they don’t even try to stop. Therefore, you need to convince them that worry, like guilt and fear, is nothing more than an emotion, and like all emotions, is subject to the power of the will. Tell them that they can eliminate worry from their lives by simply refusing to attend to it. Explain to them that if they refuse to act worried __________, they will eventually stop feeling worried and will begin to experience the contentment that accompanies a worry-free life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 감정과 무관하게(regardless of how they feel) 걱정하는 척하기를 거부하면 걱정이 사라진다
det.analysis:
❌ ① only when they feel calm: '차분할 때만'이라면 걱정될 때는 그대로 걱정하게 되므로 글의 방법(감정과 무관하게 행동)과 모순
❌ ② as soon as others notice: '남이 알아채자마자'는 본문에 없는 조건
❌ ③ before the problem appears: '문제가 생기기 전'이라는 시점 조건은 문맥과 무관
✅ ④ regardless of how they feel: 원문 일치. 기분이 어떻든 '상관없이' 걱정하는 척을 거부하면 결국 걱정이 멈춘다는 핵심 논지에 부합 ←정답
det.tip: refuse to act worried regardless of how they feel = 기분과 무관하게 걱정하는 척 거부
